review_type: Independent cross-review; not a blinded or fresh-context benchmark
input_boundary: Reviewed the supplied HTML, original holdout brief, indicated skill and actual browser observations only. No handoffs, author conclusions, earlier case outputs or evaluation notes were read for this review.
summary: The actual bicycle has a strong role, configuration choices and quote data operate accurately, and enlarged controls/totals reflow. No decorative indicator lights or ordinary-action arrows were found, including SVG and pseudo-elements. One low-priority artwork placement/contrast issue remains.

remaining_issues.location: #bicycle-illustration > text (the pale Kite decal at x=546, y=320, rotated -31 degrees)
remaining_issues.condition: Normal desktop render with Ochre and Forest selected; visible in magnified actual-browser captures
remaining_issues.observation: The pale Kite wordmark is positioned just above the diagonal frame tube, on the pale page background, rather than on the painted tube. The close-ups show the letters floating above the frame. Its #f6f4df fill against #f1f3ed is approximately 1.01:1, so it nearly disappears at ordinary size.
remaining_issues.consequence: This small illustration detail looks detached from the physical bicycle and loses legibility. It does not prevent identifying or configuring the product because the main Kite brand and current paint labels remain clear.
remaining_issues.correction: Align and size the decal as a mark on the actual tube, then check its contrast against all three paint choices; alternatively remove the nonessential decal. Preserve the original bicycle geometry and do not add a backing pill or decorative arrow.
remaining_issues.boundary: This is a concrete placement/legibility problem in an otherwise justified illustration role, not evidence that brand marks or detailed bicycle artwork are generic.

signal_review.observation_and_reason: The rectangular size choices, paint samples and radio choices are actual configuration controls. Selected fills/borders reflect real choices; none is an ornamental status pill.

No italic font treatment occurs. The small SVG brand decal is rotated to follow the diagonal tube; rotation is an illustration-placement role, not an italic headline accent. Its registration issue is R1.
Instrument Serif is absent. The interface uses system sans-serif stacks, with Arial for the SVG decal. No font substitution is indicated.
No negative letter spacing is authored or apparent. Headings, totals and quote values reflow under enlarged text without colliding.

The controls, selected outputs, totals and summary operate on the supplied choices. There are no fabricated reviews, availability claims, delivery claims, performance metrics or inactive commerce controls.
Sections use spacing rather than repeated horizontal rules. The Configure underline is a navigation affordance; control borders and focus outlines are not redundant section dividers.

The interface colors have clear text, surface, selection and paint roles. The dark translucent backdrop communicates modality. R1 is a localized exception: the pale decal lies on the similarly pale page, with about 1.01:1 contrast; correct its placement/actual background relationship instead of globally darkening the palette.
The borders identify actual size choices, selected paint and actionable buttons. They do not fragment ordinary content into equal-priority boxed cards. Preserve control and focus boundaries.

The original side-view bicycle is the product illustration explicitly requested by the brief. Spokes, rims, chain and frame make the object recognizable; they are not a fake technical dashboard or diagram. The adjacent note explicitly limits component/proportion accuracy, so the drawing is not presented as an additional specification.

Model, headline and description each add distinct supplied information. The preview label binds the actual painted object to the current color; proposal, estimate and no-payment notices preserve honest boundaries. Repeating current data in the quote is the requested review task, not duplicate framing.
No source paths or fake implementation labels decorate the page. Everyday / 01 is the supplied model name, not a code breadcrumb.
There is no ornamental section sequence. The 01 belongs to the supplied model name and should be preserved; prices are actual configuration data.

Fieldset legends label actual choices and selected outputs confirm current values. The preview caption and quote model identify their distinct content. There is no repeated eyebrow-heading-description scaffold.
No ASCII or terminal-style imagery occurs. The bicycle is actual original SVG geometry.

Curves depict the brake cable, fork, saddle, chain and wheel geometry. The flat ground shadow places the object. These marks are assigned to the bicycle illustration, not free-floating doodles or ornamental emphasis.
No monospace font is used. Tabular numeric settings stabilize prices in an ordinary sans-serif face; they are meaningful data formatting, not a technical costume.
Supporting labels are sentence case. GBP is the real currency abbreviation, not repeated all-caps scaffolding. The decal reads Kite in normal title case.
There are no gradient backgrounds or SVG gradient fills. Solid strokes/highlights articulate the illustrative bicycle material, rather than ambient haze behind the interface.
Buttons and short navigation labels do not carry ornamental periods. The supplied headline and descriptive/disclaimer sentences keep normal punctuation.

No decorative activity, availability, demo or brand lights occur. The wheel-option circles are native radio controls with real selection meaning; circular hubs/rims belong to the bicycle object. Paint samples communicate the supplied color choices. None should be removed merely because it is a small colored shape.

signal_review.signal: Additional default: arrow glyphs and icons
signal_review.observation_and_reason: No ordinary action or caption has an appended arrow or chevron. The cable, handlebar, crank and derailleur paths depict bicycle parts rather than drawn arrows. Pseudo-element inspection found no generated before/after content.

enlarged_observations.method: All HTML computed font sizes at 200%, with container em relationships included; SVG artwork remains proportionally unchanged
